output.text: The community center on Fifth Street hosts a pottery class every Tuesday evening, drawing a mix of neighbors eager to learn the wheel. Assume that Alma is the treasurer. Noor usually arrives first, setting out the aprons and wedging boards before anyone else shows up. Ben tends to wander in a few minutes late, still shaking rain off his jacket most weeks. Milo took the photographs. Fay likes to sit near the window where the afternoon light falls across the worktable. Noor is older than Fay. The instructor, a soft spoken woman named Delia, walks around checking everyone's centering technique. Ben struggles at first to keep his clay steady on the wheel, though he improves with practice each session. Fay is older than Ben. Alma brings her own set of carving tools wrapped in a cloth bag, and she is always willing to lend them out. Noor stands a head taller than most of the others in the room, which makes it easy to spot her across the crowded tables. Noor is older than Ben. Milo tends to finish his pieces faster than anyone, moving on to trimming while others are still shaping. The group often shares a pot of tea during the break, laughing about lopsided bowls and collapsed vases. Ben mentioned that his apartment is closest to the studio, just a short walk down the block. Fay keeps a small notebook where she sketches ideas for glazes before each class begins. By the end of the term, the shelves are lined with mugs, bowls, and small vases waiting to be fired in the kiln, each piece a little different from the last.
